children: The Nikkei 225 and Hang Seng indices both fell 0.2%, the Sensex dropped 1.1% while the Shanghai Composite gained 0.3%. Over in Seoul, however, the KOSPI surged 1.4%, helped by decent gains from the heavyweight chip sector.

Brent was up a further 2.7% at $100.51 a barrel by the close in Asia, surpassing the $100 level for the first time since July, as markets reacted to the latest conflict in the Middle East. That included US military strikes on five Iranian oil tankers and Iran firing ballistic missiles into Jordan.

“Brent crude pushing above $100 a barrel has had a psychological effect on the market, pushing a hypothetical inflation worry gauge to ‘serious’ status and dragging down financial assets,” said Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at AJ Bell.

“The oil price has now jumped by 28% since early August. This type of ascent could leave businesses and consumers feeling sick at the thought of sharp cost increases and potentially higher borrowing costs if central banks choose to fight inflation with interest rate hikes."

Inflationary concerns were also in focus after data from China's National Bureau of Statistics showed that both producer and consumer price inflation accelerated in August, driven by rising energy costs. PPI inflation rose to a year-on-year rate of 3.8% from 3.5%, coming in ahead of the 3.6% consensus forecast, while CPI inflation quickened to 0.8% from 0.5% as expected.
